Mobile and other platform parity, preview behavior and any reduction in tab creation were not verified.

features.title: Profiles as Apps
features.description: Orion documents separate browsing profiles with their own extensions, cookies and settings, presented through its Profiles as Apps workflow.
limitations: Scoped to the 1.0 announcement; equivalent behavior on iOS/iPadOS or other platforms was not established.
Profile boundaries and extension behavior were not runtime- or security-tested.

features.title: Mini Toolbar, Overflow Menu and Page Tweak
features.description: The 1.0 announcement documents user-selectable compact interface controls and per-page presentation controls through Mini Toolbar, Overflow Menu and Page Tweak.
limitations: The announcement does not establish identical controls on every mobile or desktop edition.
No usability, focus-visibility or resource-use comparison was run; compact UI is not a measured engine-performance advantage.

features.title: Built-in content blocking and privacy defaults
features.description: Orion's 1.0 announcement documents built-in content-blocking controls and privacy-oriented defaults.
limitations: Control presence is documentary; blocking effectiveness and the publisher's zero-telemetry assertion were not independently audited.
Defaults and feature parity across mobile, desktop and later releases were not tested.

features.title: GNOME-native interface
features.description: GNOME Web documents an interface following the GNOME Human Interface Guidelines, with desktop integration and limited exposed technical detail for nontechnical users.
platforms: Linux, primarily GNOME and similar desktops
limitations: Design intent and project documentation are not a measured usability result.
Native portability to other operating systems and identical behavior across stable, Technology Preview and Canary channels were not established.

features.title: Optional Firefox Sync integration
features.description: The README documents optional encrypted synchronization through Mozilla's Firefox Sync service and explicitly distinguishes GNOME Web from Firefox or Mozilla endorsement.
limitations: Service integration and encryption are documented claims, not a synchronization or cryptographic audit.
Coverage across distribution packages, channels and engine versions was not tested.

features.title: Tracking prevention and filter-list ad blocking
features.description: GNOME Web documents Intelligent Tracking Prevention enabled by default and filter-list-based advertisement blocking.
limitations: Documented defaults do not establish measured tracking prevention or blocking effectiveness.
Distribution, channel and WebKitGTK differences were not tested; no cross-platform parity is claimed.

features.title: Reader mode
features.description: NEWS documents reader-mode presentation and correctness work, including line-spacing improvements.
limitations: The rolling release history supplies capability evidence, not a claim that reader mode was first introduced in 51.2.
No page extraction, readability, accessibility or package-specific behavior was tested.

features.title: Installed web-app background and quit controls
features.description: The 50.0 NEWS entry documents a configurable background-running toggle and quit action for installed web apps, including operation outside Flatpak.
limitations: Version-scoped release documentation, not a lifecycle or web-app compatibility test.
The non-Flatpak statement does not establish equivalent behavior in every distribution package or channel.

features.title: Built-in AdBlock plugin
features.description: Falkon's About page documents a built-in AdBlock plugin enabled by default.
platforms: Windows (nightly distribution documented; feature parity unverified)
limitations: Project-level documentation was not verified against a binary or measured blocking workload.
Windows nightly distribution is not proof of equal stable-channel support or per-platform defaults.

features.title: VerticalTabs plugin
features.description: Falkon's release history documents a VerticalTabs plugin with tree and collapse behavior, plus keyboard and tab-switching improvements.
platforms: Windows (nightly distribution documented; plugin availability unverified)
limitations: Capability evidence comes from a CHANGELOG whose top entry is 25.08.0; it is not a 26.08.3 feature test.
Plugin availability, defaults and behavior across platforms or packages were not established by runtime testing.

features.title: Userscripts, Python plugins and QML plugins
features.description: The CHANGELOG documents GreaseMonkey userscript support and Python and QML plugin mechanisms.
platforms: Windows (nightly distribution documented; plugin availability unverified)
limitations: These documented mechanisms do not establish complete Chrome Web Store or WebExtensions compatibility.
Historical release entries were not exercised on current builds; dependency, package and OS-specific availability remain unverified.

features.title: Per-site settings and permissions
features.description: Falkon's release history documents per-site user-agent and cookie controls and later permission management for unknown protocols.
platforms: Windows (nightly distribution documented; feature parity unverified)
limitations: The inspected CHANGELOG ends at a top entry of 25.08.0, rather than providing complete 26.08.3 coverage.
No permission enforcement, persistence, protocol handling or per-platform behavior was tested.

features.title: KWallet and Plasma integration
features.description: Falkon's CHANGELOG documents KWallet password storage and Plasma download integration.
limitations: Desktop-specific release-history evidence does not establish availability on Windows, macOS or every Linux desktop.
No password-store, download workflow or current-package integration was exercised.

features.title: Vim-style keyboard navigation
features.description: The quickstart documents hjkl navigation, history traversal, tab switching and keyboard URL or search entry.
limitations: Instructions were read, not timed or tested with international keyboard layouts or assistive technology.
Documented distribution platforms do not establish identical bindings or behavior in every package; other community ports retain package/backend caveats.

features.title: Link and element hints
features.description: The quickstart documents pressing f to show letter hints for mouse-free activation; 3.6.0 release notes add hints in open shadow DOMs.
limitations: The shadow-DOM addition is version-scoped documentary evidence, not a test of all pages, elements or Qt builds.
Input conflicts, focus restoration, keyboard layouts and assistive-technology behavior were not tested; keyboard operation alone does not establish accessibility conformance.

features.title: Command line and contextual help
features.description: The quickstart documents : to open the command line, :help for in-product documentation and per-command --help.
limitations: No command was executed and no discovery-time or learning-curve comparison was performed.
Command availability can depend on release and package; per-platform equivalence was not established.

features.title: Keyboard tab and session control
features.description: The quickstart documents closing and undo-closing tabs, saving open tabs on quit and configurable session saving through keyboard-oriented workflows.
limitations: No close, restore, quit or session-persistence behavior was exercised.
Documentation does not establish identical session behavior across every platform, backend or package.

features.title: File-oriented bookmark and quickmark reload
features.description: The 3.7.0 changelog adds :quickmark-reload and :bookmark-reload so externally changed collections can be reloaded.
limitations: These commands are attributed to the released 3.7.0 entry, not the explicitly unreleased 3.8.0 entry.
No collection files were changed or commands run; packaging and platform-specific behavior remain untested.

features.title: Reconfigurable Lisp command environment
features.description: Nyxt documents Emacs, vi and CUA bindings together with runtime Lisp introspection and customization.
platforms: Linux x86-64 (5.0.0 release asset; feature parity unverified)
macOS ARM64 (5.0.0 release asset; feature parity unverified)
limitations: Command-layer descriptions come from README/FAQ documentation; CEF is the default in 5.0.0 and WebKitGTK remains an alternative, without tested backend parity.
Assets establish distribution, not successful execution or identical features. Native Windows availability and learning-curve or efficiency benefits were not established.

features.title: Fuzzy buffer switching and multi-object commands
features.description: The README documents fuzzy buffer selection and commands accepting multiple inputs, such as several bookmarks or other objects for one operation.
platforms: Linux x86-64 (5.0.0 release asset; feature parity unverified)
macOS ARM64 (5.0.0 release asset; feature parity unverified)
limitations: README behavior was not executed on the 5.0.0 CEF default or alternate WebKitGTK backend.
Release assets do not establish OS/backend parity, action-scope predictability or error recovery.

features.title: Multi-tab search with a unified results view
features.description: The README describes searching multiple open tabs at the same time and displaying all results in a single window.
platforms: Linux x86-64 (5.0.0 release asset; feature parity unverified)
macOS ARM64 (5.0.0 release asset; feature parity unverified)
limitations: Search coverage and retrieval behavior were not exercised on the 5.0.0 CEF default or alternate WebKitGTK backend.
Platform parity and the relationship to current Chrome tab-title/URL or content-search behavior were not established.

features.title: Tagged bookmarks and compound queries
features.description: Nyxt's README documents bookmark tags and compound queries for user-organized collections beyond a folder-only workflow.
platforms: Linux x86-64 (5.0.0 release asset; feature parity unverified)
macOS ARM64 (5.0.0 release asset; feature parity unverified)
limitations: Bookmark and query behavior was not tested on either documented 5.0.0 platform or across CEF and WebKitGTK backends.
No retrieval-efficiency comparison or claim about Chrome feature absence is established.

features.title: 5.0 CEF extension and request-blocking integration
features.description: The 5.0.0 release makes CEF the default and documents loading unpacked Chromium Manifest V2/V3 extensions, extension-management commands and request blocking using uBlock Origin default filter lists.
platforms: Linux x86-64 (5.0.0 CEF release; per-platform behavior unverified)
macOS ARM64 (5.0.0 CEF release; per-platform behavior unverified)
limitations: Version- and renderer-scoped documentation; alternate WebKitGTK behavior is not assumed equivalent, and Electron was removed in 5.0.0.
No extension was loaded or blocker tested. Manifest support and use of filter lists do not prove every Chromium extension or uBlock feature works.

features.title: Independent web-platform stack
features.description: Ladybird documents its own LibWeb rendering, LibJS JavaScript and LibWasm WebAssembly implementation rather than a Blink, Gecko or WebKit fork.
limitations: Pre-alpha architecture for developers, not complete standards conformance or consumer readiness; third-party libraries are still used.
No build or site-compatibility test was run. Other Unix-like and WSL2 paths do not establish feature parity or a native Windows browser release.

features.title: Site-separated sandboxed renderer processes
features.description: Ladybird's README describes a multi-process design in which documents from different sites run in separate renderer processes sandboxed from the rest of the system.
limitations: A documented pre-alpha architecture, not an independently validated sandbox or security comparison.
Per-platform isolation behavior, other documented build paths and native Windows browser support were not tested or established as equivalent.

features.title: Out-of-process helper work
features.description: The README documents out-of-process work for networking, image decoding, compositing and media.
limitations: The project remains pre-alpha and developer-targeted; architecture descriptions do not establish complete media or website support.
No process, performance or per-platform implementation behavior was inspected at runtime.

features.title: User-configured content-blocker lists
features.description: Ladybird's FAQ documents user-configured content-blocker lists.
limitations: A pre-alpha documented capability, not an effectiveness or per-platform test.
Discussion of future uBlock extension support is not implemented extension compatibility or a released consumer-browser milestone.

features.title: WebView embedding API
features.description: Servo documents a WebView API for embedding web content in applications through its modular Rust-based engine.
limitations: Servo is a prototype engine; the listed project targets do not establish equal embedding API coverage or release-binary support.
No embedding integration, build or performance comparison was run; embeddability is distinct from a complete end-user browser.

features.title: WebGL and version-qualified WebGPU work
features.description: Servo's homepage describes WebGL and WebGPU support. Its July progress report, covering 0.5.0, specifically documents WebGPU work behind dom_webgpu_enabled.
limitations: Graphics completeness and current defaults were not established for each project platform; the historical flag statement is not an all-version default claim.
Experimental engine documentation only; no graphics, GPU, compatibility or performance tests were run.

features.title: Keyboard navigation milestones
features.description: The March progress update documents Tab navigation, accesskey activation with Alt+Shift and scrolling with Space or Shift+Space.
limitations: Version-scoped prototype-engine progress, not complete browser keyboard support or assistive-technology conformance.
No keyboard interaction was run; desktop equivalence, mobile behavior and the separate FreeBSD build milestone were not validated.

features.title: Firefox DevTools Console autocomplete
features.description: The July update, describing 0.5.0 work, documents basic Console autocomplete when Firefox DevTools is connected to Servo.
limitations: Basic autocomplete is one documented prototype capability, not complete DevTools compatibility.
No debugger connection or Console session was run; availability across current builds and operating systems remains unverified.

features.title: 0.8.0 input and accessibility implementation milestones
features.description: Visible 0.8.0 release entries include beforeinput, double/triple-click selection extension, ARIA-to-AccessKit role mapping, focused-node work and WebDriver computed-role support.
limitations: These are specific implementation milestones in a prototype/tech demo, not comprehensive input, screen-reader or accessibility conformance.
Release notes were truncated to visible entries; no current-platform parity or runtime behavior was tested.
OpenHarmony artifacts are not automatically signed for HarmonyOS, and later selection work supersedes earlier future-facing selection statements.

features.title: Selective image loading and optional panel hiding
features.description: The manual documents images-off mode using alt text or placeholders, loading individual images on demand and hiding browser panels.
limitations: Manual evidence is from v3.2.0-90-g29a46a2d; platform names describe project scope, not per-platform feature tests.
No image-loading, resource-saving or usability measurement was performed. The documented renderer has limited HTML/CSS and no JavaScript.

features.title: Reading-oriented scrolling
features.description: Dillo documents page-at-a-time scrollbar navigation, configurable page overlap and an optional left-side scrollbar; the 3.2.0 notes describe book-like scrolling.
limitations: Historical release and manual documentation, not a current all-platform behavior test.
No readability, focus or scrolling-efficiency comparison was run; constrained web-platform coverage changes comparison workloads.

features.title: Offline help and keyboard command discovery
features.description: Dillo documents offline help, the 3.3.0 about:keys page, numbered tab shortcuts and copy, zoom and navigation controls.
limitations: The about:keys addition is sourced to 3.3.0; other controls come from the earlier generated manual.
No key handling, offline operation or assistive-technology behavior was exercised on any listed platform.

features.title: Standard-input/output protocol plugins
features.description: The canonical site documents protocol plugins written in different languages and communicating through standard input/output, with examples including Gemini, Gopher, IPFS and man-page browsing.
limitations: Examples do not establish that every plugin is installed, maintained or supported in each platform package.
No plugin was installed or executed; protocol coverage, security and external dependencies were not tested.

features.title: 3.3.0 dilloc control and page actions
features.description: The 3.3.0 notes document dilloc commands over a local UNIX socket for open, reload, readiness and dump operations, plus configurable page-menu actions integrating external tools.
limitations: No local-control command, socket or external-tool action was executed; the interface is not evidence of safe agent integration.
Windows/Cygwin and Atari support for this specific interface was not established.
The same release qualifies FLTK 1.4 as experimental with HiDPI/Wayland problems; no build configuration was validated.

features.title: Arrow and numbered-target navigation
features.description: The users guide documents arrow/numeric navigation and numbering links and form fields for direct selection.
limitations: Guide instructions were read through bounded excerpts, not executed in any terminal or OS variant.
Keyboard coverage does not establish screen-reader accessibility or graphical modern-web parity; historical port lists are not a current support matrix.

features.title: In-context help and keymap
features.description: Lynx documents ? or H for help and K for current commands and key bindings while viewing a document.
limitations: No help, keymap or discovery-time behavior was tested.
Terminal key handling, configuration and build differences remain unverified across platforms.

features.title: Forms and configurable text entry
features.description: The users guide documents forms and text entry, including external textarea editing and configurable line-editing or key styles.
limitations: No form, external editor or OS-specific integration was exercised.
Documented terminal forms do not establish compatibility with JavaScript-dependent or rich graphical application workflows.

features.title: Formatted text, source and link-list output
features.description: The manual documents -dump formatted text output, source output, link-only output and configurable output width.
limitations: CLI documentation was inspected in bounded excerpts; no command or pipeline was run.
Output, encoding and option availability were not verified for every build; text output is not pixel-equivalent rendering of a modern web application.

features.title: Local files, network protocols and character controls
features.description: Lynx documentation covers local files and multiple network protocols alongside character-set and language controls.
limitations: Historical protocol and platform lists do not establish support in every current build.
The maintainer explicitly distinguishes Windows variants without OpenSSL that cannot connect to HTTPS URLs.
No file, protocol, encoding or language behavior was tested.

features.title: Combined browser and pager workflow
features.description: The inspected maintained-fork documentation describes displaying files or standard input and rendering HTML to standard output with -dump.
platforms: Unix-like systems (historical maintained-fork documentation; current OS coverage unverified)
limitations: Documentary capability only; no terminal command or pipeline was executed.
The README and manpage have historical dates. Overall upstream lifecycle and current distribution/platform support remain unknown.

features.title: Keyboard buffers and tabs
features.description: The maintained-fork manual and tab documentation describe buffers, tabs, tab-selection menus and user-overridable key bindings.
platforms: Unix-like systems (historical maintained-fork documentation; current OS coverage unverified)
limitations: No key binding, terminal interaction or tab workflow was tested; some documented functions have no default binding.
Historical documentation does not settle current per-platform support or the project's unknown overall upstream lifecycle.

features.title: Text layout for HTML tables and frames
features.description: The inspected manual documents text layout for HTML tables and frames rather than simply stripping all markup.
platforms: Unix-like systems (historical maintained-fork documentation; current OS coverage unverified)
limitations: The same manual says JavaScript and CSS are ignored; this is not equivalent rendering of interactive graphical applications.
No layout tests were run. Build/platform behavior and overall upstream lifecycle remain unverified or unknown.

features.title: Optional inline graphics and external image viewing
features.description: The inspected documentation describes optional inline graphics using w3m-img or a sixel-enabled setup, with external image viewers as another documented route.
platforms: Unix-like systems (compatible terminal, build and external tools required; current OS coverage unverified)
limitations: Graphics depend on terminal support, build configuration and optional external dependencies; no dependency was installed or graphics path tested.
Historical documentation establishes neither current native macOS/Windows packaging nor active overall upstream maintenance; lifecycle remains unknown.

features.title: Explicit graphical-browser URL handoff
features.description: The maintained-fork manual documents sending the current target URL to a graphical browser with a command when text rendering is inadequate.
platforms: Unix-like systems (historical maintained-fork documentation; current OS coverage unverified)
limitations: No handoff or external browser was launched; configuration, destination-browser and per-platform behavior were not tested.
A URL handoff is a complementary workflow, not proof of shared session state or modern-web equivalence. Overall upstream lifecycle remains unknown.

recommendationCandidates.title: Separate product kind, engine, platform, channel and lifecycle
recommendationCandidates.description: Prevent prototype engines, terminal pagers and constrained browsers from appearing as unqualified drop-in Chrome replacements. Count engine families separately from browser brands.
verificationNeeded: Check that experimental, unofficial, discontinued and released platform states remain visible in comparison views.
Check that backend changes are scoped to versions.
limitations: A tracker-design proposal, not evidence that Chrome lacks a feature.

recommendationCandidates.title: Preserve dates, short quotes, claim types and version scope per fact
recommendationCandidates.description: Keep retrieval dates separate from release dates, retain null for unknown publication dates, and surface source conflicts rather than silently selecting generic metadata.
verificationNeeded: Verify citations against the decisive body text.
Prevent a roadmap, copyright year, repository creation date or empty RSS date from becoming a release claim.
limitations: Data-governance recommendation derived from this lane's documentary findings.

recommendationCandidates.title: Evaluate keyboard task completion and command discoverability
recommendationCandidates.description: Compare in-product command/key references and searchable actions using qutebrowser help, Nyxt introspection, Lynx keymaps and Dillo about:keys as documented design examples.
verificationNeeded: Establish current Chrome native and explicitly disclosed extension baselines.
Measure discovery time, completion time and recovery errors for URL entry, tab switching, close/undo-close and finding commands.
Evaluate assistive technology separately from keyboard shortcut coverage.
limitations: No current Chrome feature absence or speed advantage was established.

recommendationCandidates.title: Evaluate opt-in target hints and multi-object commands
recommendationCandidates.description: Use qutebrowser letter hints, Lynx numbered targets and Nyxt multiple marking as alternative interaction models, with explicit action scope and predictable escape behavior.
verificationNeeded: Compare against current Chrome and disclosed extension configurations.
Test inputs, dialogs, shadow DOM, page shortcut conflicts, focus restoration, zoom and international keyboard layouts.
Measure errors and task completion rather than shortcut counts alone.
limitations: Untested proposal; keyboard-first is not proof of accessibility compliance or a missing Chrome capability.

recommendationCandidates.title: Evaluate lightweight reading controls with matched workloads
recommendationCandidates.description: Compare focus/compact interfaces, clear profile identity, selective image loading and page-overlap scrolling. Keep UI density, rendering feature coverage and resource use as separate measures.
verificationNeeded: Establish current Chrome reading, profile and app-window behavior first.
Measure task completion, readability, retained functions, CPU/RAM/network use and restore/exit behavior on matching content.
Make background-running state and active identity understandable.
limitations: No lighter-than-Chrome measurement exists here.
A browser that omits JavaScript does not provide an equivalent workload for a modern web application.

recommendationCandidates.title: Provide semantic HTML and a useful text/no-JavaScript reading path
recommendationCandidates.description: Keep the research readable with headings, descriptive links, linear reading order and text-oriented export, drawing on Lynx and w3m's documented workflows.
verificationNeeded: Verify meaningful navigation and source citations without JavaScript.
Check tables and reading order in a text-oriented view and with assistive technology.
limitations: Recommendation for the tracker, not an assertion that terminal browsers replace Chrome for interactive applications.
No frontend build or browser QA was conducted in this lane.

recommendationCandidates.title: Maintain a versioned engine-diversity and interoperability watchlist
recommendationCandidates.description: Track independent implementations and WebKit-based products alongside shared-Chromium shells. Separate standards conformance, embedding APIs, security architecture and consumer readiness.
verificationNeeded: Collect dated standards/compatibility results and small reproducible cases before asserting interoperability gaps.
Compare performance only on matching tasks with equivalent enabled functionality.
limitations: No WPT run or current Chrome comparison was performed.
Experimental readiness is preserved even when a repository publishes a non-prerelease version tag.

recommendationCandidates.title: Version platform support independently of product-wide health
recommendationCandidates.description: Keep a dated support history per platform and channel, independently of the overall product lifecycle. Orion's continuing Apple development coexists with ended Kagi Linux/Windows work; native releases, unofficial ports, WSL/Cygwin paths and experimental targets need distinct support states.
verificationNeeded: Check that a product-wide active label cannot erase Orion's platform-specific Kagi cessation and unknown successor stewardship.
Retain effective dates, version/channel scope and citations for each support transition; distinguish native releases from WSL/Cygwin or unofficial paths.
Verify that experimental or unknown platform support stays visible without inferring readiness from a release asset, future roadmap or downstream package.
Establish a current Chrome platform/channel baseline before making any comparative support claim.
limitations: Tracker-design proposal grounded in documentary lifecycle differences; no current Chrome support or feature-parity assessment was performed.
Orion's successor handoff, Nyxt native Windows readiness and w3m overall upstream lifecycle remain unresolved in the saved evidence.

recommendationCandidates.title: Evaluate link-preview effort and tab proliferation
recommendationCandidates.description: Use Orion's documented Link Preview, including links originating in other applications, as a design example for measuring the effort to inspect linked content before opening a full tab.
verificationNeeded: Establish current Chrome native, platform-specific and explicitly disclosed extension preview behavior before classifying a gap.
Compare inspection time, actions and tabs created on matched in-browser and external-application link tasks.
Check dismiss/escape behavior, focus restoration and the transition from preview to full tab on each evaluated platform.
limitations: Orion's 1.0 announcement supplies the design example; mobile parity and later-version behavior were not established.
No runtime preview test, tab-count measurement or current Chrome parity assessment was performed.

recommendationCandidates.title: Evaluate cross-tab content retrieval separately from title and URL search
recommendationCandidates.description: Use Nyxt's documented multi-tab search and unified results view to evaluate retrieval across open-page content. Keep this task distinct from finding a tab by its title or URL and from selecting multiple objects for a command.
verificationNeeded: Establish the content actually searched by Nyxt and the current Chrome native/extension baseline, separately from tab-title/URL search.
Measure completion time and retrieval errors on tasks whose answers occur in page content but not in tab titles or URLs.
Check result-to-page navigation, highlighted context, escape behavior and disclosed scope when tabs are unloaded or page content changes.
Record the tested platform, Nyxt release and CEF or WebKitGTK backend rather than assuming 5.0.0 backend or platform parity.
limitations: The saved README documents searching multiple tabs, but indexing scope, result coverage and runtime behavior were not tested.
This is a retrieval-evaluation hypothesis; no current Chrome feature absence or measured advantage was established.

recommendationCandidates.title: Evaluate plugin and desktop workflows with engine-update awareness
recommendationCandidates.description: Use Falkon's documented plugin options, KWallet storage and Plasma download integration as examples for comparing coherent UI and desktop workflows. Record the actual QtWebEngine/Chromium backend version and update channel alongside the product version; a smaller toolbar does not establish a smaller engine footprint.
verificationNeeded: Establish current Chrome native and disclosed-extension behavior for the same plugin, password-store and download tasks on the same desktop.
Verify which documented Falkon plugins and desktop integrations are supplied by each evaluated package; distinguish KDE/Plasma integration from Windows nightly distribution.
Record actual browser and engine versions, package provenance, update responsibility and channel before comparing update freshness or support.
Measure UI workflow effort separately from CPU, memory and retained page functionality; do not infer engine resource use from toolbar density.
limitations: Falkon capability details come from release history topped by 25.08.0, while its feed lists 26.08.3 without a verified publication date.
No plugin, desktop integration, engine update or resource benchmark was exercised; current Chrome parity is unknown.
qutebrowser bundle/update documentation illustrates package-specific engine boundaries and does not establish Falkon's installed engine version.

recommendationCandidates.title: Evaluate text and pipeline export with graceful graphical handoff
recommendationCandidates.description: Use w3m's browser/pager, standard-input/output and explicit graphical-browser URL handoff workflows, alongside Lynx text/link output, as complementary browser-workflow evaluation ideas. Assess moving useful content through a text pipeline and opening a target graphically when text rendering is inadequate.
verificationNeeded: Establish current Chrome native and explicitly disclosed extension behavior for text/link export and browser handoff before proposing a missing capability.
Check meaningful text, links, encoding and source context on matched export/pipeline tasks, including disclosure of omitted interactive content.
Verify target URL fidelity, explicit destination choice and graceful fallback to graphical viewing when text is insufficient; measure effort and errors.
Record terminal, package, OS and destination-browser conditions, and test session/authentication behavior rather than assuming state transfers with a URL.
limitations: This browser-workflow proposal is distinct from the existing semantic-HTML recommendation for the research site.
The inspected w3m documentation ignores JavaScript and CSS; text output is not an equivalent modern interactive application workload.
No pipeline or handoff was executed, current Chrome parity is unknown, and w3m's overall upstream lifecycle remains unknown.
